sentences.en: I think it's fair to say, even though he hasn't appeared in the rest of his history, he will be a great friend of the rest of his history, Sir John Falstaff.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，因为哈尔王子据说是和法斯塔夫以及奇普赛德的所有小伙子们一起狂欢什么的。

sentences.en: Yeah, because Prince Hal is off supposedly wassailing with Falstaff and all the lads down in Cheapside and everything.
sentences.zh: 所以这些剧作之所以如此精彩的原因之一，就是你确实有很多，你知道的，威斯特摩兰伯爵带着八十人冲进来之类的情节。

sentences.zh: 但你也有这些关于伦敦阴暗面生活的不可思议的写照，还有这位极其有趣的形象，法斯塔夫，

sentences.zh: 只是想说，如果人们还没有看过或读过这两部剧中的任何一部，

sentences.zh: 还有让娜·莫罗看起来非常迷人，像个时髦女郎。

sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 它真的非常非常棒。

sentences.zh: 它真的很精彩。

sentences.en: It's really brilliant.
sentences.zh: 总之，绝对是我最喜欢的电影之一。

sentences.en: Anyway, so absolutely one of my favourite filMs.

sentences.en: Henry IV, part one and two, my favourite plays.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常期待这个系列。

sentences.en: So hugely looking forward to this.
sentences.zh: 如果人们真的很感兴趣，还有一个BBC版本叫《空王冠》，采用了那些台词。

sentences.zh: 我期待这里有顶级的表现，因为我们通过谈论圆屋剧场和汤姆·希德勒斯顿等等，已经把标准定得很高了。

sentences.en: I'm expecting a top performance here because we've set the bar very high with the talk of the roundhouse and Tom Hiddleston and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 好吧，没压力。

sentences.zh: 所以你将带我们了解它，但这里有一个悖论，不是吗？

sentences.en: So you're going to be taking us through it, but there's a paradox here, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 那就是《亨利四世（上篇）》和《下篇》是非常著名的剧作，

sentences.en: Which is that Henry IV, parts one and two are very famous plays,
sentences.zh: 但亨利四世本人却是一个稍微有点冷门的人物，对于我们的许多听众以及我猜对于许多海外听众来说，

sentences.en: but Henry IV himself is a slightly obscure figure and will be to a lot of our listeners and to many of our overseas listeners, I'm guessing,
sentences.zh: 可能从来没听说过他，对他也没有什么概念。

sentences.en: will probably never have heard of him and have no sense of him.
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: Why is that, do you think?
sentences.zh: 当他实际上有一个如此有趣的故事时，他推翻了他的堂兄，他夺取了王冠，他是一个篡位者，他缺乏安全感，他的儿子后来成为了伟大的英雄国王。

sentences.en: When he's actually got such an interesting story, he topples his cousin, he takes the crown, he's a usurper, he's insecure, his son goes on to be the great hero king.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们对亨利四世了解不多？

sentences.en: Why don't we know more about Henry IV?
sentences.zh: 这确实很有趣，因为在《亨利四世》剧中，我是说，他是一个相当模糊的人物。

sentences.en: It is interesting because in the Henry IV plays, I mean, he's quite a shadowy figure.
sentences.zh: 他看起来非常疲惫。

sentences.en: He's very kind of weary.
sentences.zh: 他忧心忡忡。

sentences.en: He's careworn.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他几乎与席卷英格兰的叛乱浪潮和动荡的所有伟大戏剧性无关。

sentences.en: I mean, he's almost a kind of irrelevant to all the great drama of the sweep and churn of rebellion that is convulsing England.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，总的来说，他并没有成为许多传记的主题。

sentences.zh: 所以克里斯·吉文·威尔逊的经典学术研究中说，他是英格兰中世纪晚期君主中最被忽视的一位。

sentences.en: So the classic academic study by Chris Given Wilson, Given Wilson says in that, that he's the most neglected of England's late medieval monarchs.
sentences.zh: 我想你几乎可以说他是英格兰所有君主中最被忽视的一位。

sentences.en: I think you could almost say he was the most neglected of all England's monarchs.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，他现在似乎正处于一个受关注的时刻。

sentences.en: But the interesting thing is that he seems to be having a bit of a moment right now.
sentences.zh: 所以除了吉文·威尔逊那本了不起的传记外，还有伊恩·莫蒂默写的一本，非常不错，非常易读。

sentences.en: So as well as Given Wilson's amazing biography, there's one by Ian Mortimer, which is very good, very readable.
sentences.zh: 还有海伦·卡斯托下个月即将出版的一本关于理查二世和亨利四世的精彩合传，我有机会读了，真的很好。

sentences.en: And there's a brilliant paired biography of Richard II and Henry IV by Helen Castor that is coming out next month, which I've had a chance to read, which is really good.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你对这个感兴趣，那是不容错过的。

sentences.en: So if you're interested in this, that's unmissable.

sentences.en: And I think that all these books have fixed on the fact that obviously Shakespeare did as well, that actually the story of the reign is really dramatic.
sentences.zh: 但不仅如此，他本人实际上比人们想象的要有趣得多。

sentences.en: But more than that, he himself is actually a much more interesting figure than people might think.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你所说，我是说，他掌权的故事令人难以置信。

sentences.en: So as you said, I mean, the story of his coming to power is incredible.
sentences.zh: 他从法国发动入侵并推翻了一位国王。

sentences.en: He launches an invasion from France and topples a king.
sentences.zh: 而上一位这样做的君主是威廉征服者。

sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 然后他除掉了一位国王。

sentences.en: And he then eliminates a king.
sentences.zh: 他不得不杀死理查二世。

sentences.en: So there are shades of Cromwell as well as of kind of earlier medieval regicides there, as we'll see, because it opens up a kind of constitutional can of worMs.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，我认为就他本人而言，他是一个非常非常令人印象深刻的人物。

sentences.en: But more than that, I think in and of himself, he's a very, very impressive figure.
sentences.zh: 所以在他掌权之前，他绝对被誉为英格兰伟大的骑士典范。

sentences.en: So before he comes to power, he's absolutely kind of fated as England's great model of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 他是英格兰最令人印象深刻的骑士，最著名的骑士。

sentences.en: He's the most impressive knight, the most celebrated knight in England.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为即使作为国王，由于他掌权时的环境，他的统治也非常艰难。

sentences.en: And I think even as king, because of the circumstances in which he comes to power, he has a very troubled reign.

sentences.en: And I think it would have destroyed most other men.

sentences.en: So Helen Castor, in her book, describes his grip on power throughout his reign as being white-knuckled.
sentences.zh: 有一种他为了保命而死死抓住权力的感觉。

sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但他挺过来了。

sentences.zh: 我是说，在一个非常危险的世界里，在一个非常困难的情况下，他真的令人印象深刻。

sentences.zh: 他把牌打得非常好。

sentences.zh: 但从一开始就有紧张关系。

sentences.en: But there is tension there from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们提醒自己我们身处何处，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, let's remind ourselves where we are, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以，在14世纪末的英格兰，亨利出生于1367年。

sentences.en: So, in England at the end of the 14th century, Henry was born in 1367.
sentences.zh: 他比理查二世小三个月。

sentences.en: He is three months younger than Richard II.
sentences.zh: 记得我们“百年战争”系列的听众会记得爱德华三世。

sentences.en: And people who remember our Hundred Years' War series remember Edward III.
sentences.zh: 理查二世是他年轻的继任者。

sentences.en: Richard II is his young successor.
sentences.zh: 他成为国王时还是个孩子。

sentences.en: He's a boy when he becomes king.
sentences.zh: 而且是孙子。

sentences.en: And grandson.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 所以，爱德华三世，我是说，爱德华三世有很多孩子。

sentences.en: So, Edward III, I mean, Edward III has lots of children.
sentences.zh: 他有五个儿子，但对于我们的目的，对于这个故事的目的，听众需要记住三个儿子。

sentences.en: He has five sons, but there are three sons, for our purposes, the purposes of this story, for listeners to keep in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，他有他最著名的儿子，黑太子爱德华，普瓦捷战役的胜利者，伟大的骑士典范。

sentences.en: So, he has his best-known son, Edward the Black Prince, the winner of Poitiers, the great model of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 而理查二世是黑太子的儿子。

sentences.en: And Richard II is the Black Prince's son.
sentences.zh: 然后他的第二个儿子是一个叫莱昂内尔的人，他是克拉伦斯公爵。

sentences.en: Then his second son is a guy called Lionel, who's the Duke of Clarence.
sentences.zh: 他有一个女儿，而不是儿子。

sentences.en: And he has a daughter, not a son.
sentences.zh: 而这个女儿，菲利帕，嫁给了一位非常杰出的贵族，叫埃德蒙·莫蒂默，他是马奇伯爵。

sentences.en: And this daughter, Philippa, marries a very distinguished nobleman called Edmund Mortimer, who is the Earl of March.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，他在威尔士和英格兰的边界拥有大片的土地。

sentences.en: And so, Dominic, he has a great tranche of lands and the border between Wales and England.
sentences.zh: 所以，这非常像是你的地盘。

sentences.en: So, very much your stamping ground.
sentences.zh: 我的地盘，是啊。

sentences.en: My neck of the woods, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，你本来会是他的旗手。

sentences.en: Yeah, you would have been his bannerman.
sentences.zh: 或者他本来会是我的。

sentences.en: Or he would have been mine.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为，因为当然，他娶了一位国王的孙女。

sentences.en: I don't think so, because, of course, he's married to the granddaughter of a king.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行，行，行，行，行。

sentences.en: Okay, fine, fine, fine, fine, fine.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: And they have two sons.
sentences.zh: 他们有两个儿子。

sentences.en: The elder is called Roger, and the younger, confusingly, is called Edmund.
sentences.zh: 长子叫罗杰，而次子，令人困惑的是，叫埃德蒙。

sentences.en: And Roger is seven years younger than Richard and Henry.
sentences.zh: 罗杰比理查德和亨利小七岁。

sentences.en: So, he is ahead of Henry, it might seem, in the chain of succession, except for the fact that Edward III, in 1376, had specified that his descendants, via the female line,
sentences.zh: 所以，看起来他在继承顺序上应该排在亨利前面，但爱德华三世在1376年曾明确规定，他的后代通过女性血脉，

sentences.en: shouldn't inherit the throne.
sentences.zh: 是不应该继承王位的。

sentences.en: So, that then means that Henry, who is the son of the third son of Edward III, John of Gaunt, the Duke of Lancaster.
sentences.zh: 所以，这意味着亨利，也就是爱德华三世的第三子、兰开斯特公爵冈特的约翰的儿子，

sentences.en: I mean, he's kind of behind John of Gaunt and behind Richard in the line of succession.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他在继承顺序上其实排在冈特的约翰和理查德之后。

sentences.en: But given that John of Gaunt's older, that means that Richard and Henry are natural.
sentences.zh: 但考虑到冈特的约翰年长，这意味着理查德和亨利是顺理成章的。

sentences.en: They're not rivals, but there's a kind of tension there, right?
sentences.zh: 他们不是竞争对手，但确实存在某种紧张关系，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, when Edward III dies, John of Gaunt effectively rules as regent.
sentences.zh: 所以，当爱德华三世去世时，冈特的约翰实际上是以摄政王的身份进行统治。

sentences.en: So, people who listen to our episodes on Richard II will remember that.
sentences.zh: 听过我们关于理查德二世那一集的朋友应该还记得。

sentences.en: He's a very, very impressive, controversial figure.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常、非常令人印象深刻且充满争议的人物。

sentences.en: And, effectively, it means, as you say, that Henry grows up kind of third in line to the throne.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这实际上意味着亨利在成长过程中，在王位继承顺序上排在第三位左右。

sentences.en: And so, I think that that focuses why there's an inherent awkwardness between Richard and Henry.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，这解释了为什么理查德和亨利之间存在一种固有的尴尬。

sentences.en: But I think it's also down to the fact that Henry, as this model of chivalry, he has the admiration, not just of people in England, but of people across Europe,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这也归结于这样一个事实：亨利作为骑士精神的典范，不仅受到英国人的钦佩，也受到全欧洲人的钦佩，

sentences.en: in a way that Richard doesn't.
sentences.zh: 这是理查德所没有的。

sentences.en: Richard, despite being the son of the Black Prince, he's not a model of chivalry.
sentences.zh: 理查德尽管是黑太子的儿子，但他并非骑士精神的典范。

sentences.en: He's not a man of action.
sentences.zh: 他不是一个行动派。

sentences.en: He's not galloping around doing heroic things.
sentences.zh: 他不会四处奔波去做那些英雄事迹。

sentences.en: You know, he's understandably jealous of his cousin for having the kind of the glamour.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他嫉妒他的堂兄拥有那种魅力，这是可以理解的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, just a very brief synopsis of how Henry cuts a dash in late 14th century Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想简单概述一下亨利是如何在14世纪末的欧洲大放异彩的。

sentences.en: So, his great stunt is that in 1390, he goes and attends the most famous tournament of the age, which is held just outside Calais, a place called Saint-Angelo-Vert.
sentences.zh: 他最伟大的壮举是在1390年，他参加了那个时代最著名的锦标赛，地点就在加来郊外，一个叫圣安吉洛-维尔特的地方。

sentences.en: And it is hosted by probably the most famous knight in Christendom, close contemporary of Henry's.
sentences.zh: 主办方可能是基督教世界最著名的骑士，也是亨利同时代的人。

sentences.en: And this is a guy called Jean-Lemagre, who is better known as Boussicot.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫让·勒马格，也就是大家更熟知的布西科。

sentences.en: And this is a figure that we'll be meeting throughout our story.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们在整个故事中会不断遇到的人物。

sentences.en: And he is one of three champions who have summoned a challenge to everybody to come and see if they can, you know, match them in a tournament.
sentences.zh: 他是三位冠军之一，他们向所有人发出了挑战，看看是否有人能在锦标赛中与他们一较高下。

sentences.en: And Henry leads a retinue of English champions.
sentences.zh: 亨利率领着一支由英国冠军组成的随从队伍。

sentences.en: And among this retinue of champions, there is the son of the Earl of Northumberland called Harry Percy, who has the nickname Hotspur.
sentences.zh: 在这支冠军随从队伍中，有诺森伯兰伯爵的儿子哈里·珀西，绰号“热刺”。

sentences.en: So, they go out.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们出发了。

sentences.en: They all perform very creditably.
sentences.zh: 他们都表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: Henry has 10 goes in the lists against Boussicot.
sentences.zh: 亨利在比武场上与布西科交手了10次。

sentences.en: Tremendous.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: They get on very well.
sentences.zh: 他们相处得非常好。

sentences.en: Boussicot invites him on a crusade.
sentences.zh: 布西科邀请他参加十字军东征。

sentences.en: Henry does go on a crusade.
sentences.zh: 亨利确实参加了十字军东征。

sentences.en: He goes to the Baltic to fight the pagans, the pagan Lithuanians.
sentences.zh: 他去了波罗的海与异教徒，即立陶宛异教徒作战。

sentences.en: He goes to Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 他去了耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: He gets given an ostrich in Prague.
sentences.zh: 他在布拉格获赠了一只鸵鸟。

sentences.en: He gets given a galley by the Venetians.
sentences.zh: 他从威尼斯人那里得到了一艘桨帆船。

sentences.en: He ends up going to the Holy Land.
sentences.zh: 他最终去了圣地。

sentences.en: Richard the Lionheart, Edward I, they are both kings who had been to the Holy Land, but neither of them had actually got to Jerusalem.
sentences.zh: 狮心王理查德和爱德华一世，这两位国王都曾去过圣地，但他们谁也没能真正到达耶路撒冷。

sentences.en: Henry does get into Jerusalem itself.
sentences.zh: 亨利确实进入了耶路撒冷城。

sentences.en: He goes and visits the Holy City.
sentences.zh: 他去参观了圣城。

sentences.en: And he's got a leopard.
sentences.zh: 他有一只豹子。

sentences.en: He's got a parrot.
sentences.zh: 他有一只鹦鹉。

sentences.en: He's got a leopard.
sentences.zh: 他有一只豹子。

sentences.en: He's got a parrot.
sentences.zh: 他有一只鹦鹉。

sentences.en: He's got his ostrich.
sentences.zh: 他有他的鸵鸟。

sentences.en: I mean, it's all very, very glamorous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一切都非常、非常迷人。

sentences.en: And it's unsurprisingly that back in England, people just think, this is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 毫不奇怪，在英国国内，人们都认为这太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, he's an absolute hero.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他绝对是个英雄。

sentences.en: So John Gower, who is a great poet alongside Geoffrey Chaucer, he has this poem, Confessio Amantis, and he dedicated it to Richard II.
sentences.zh: 约翰·高尔，与杰弗里·乔叟齐名的伟大诗人，他写了一首诗《恋人忏悔录》，并把它献给了理查德二世。

sentences.en: But when Henry comes back, he scrubs this dedication and dedicates it to Henry of Lancaster instead.
sentences.zh: 但当亨利回来时，他删掉了这个献词，转而把它献给了兰开斯特的亨利。

sentences.en: Henry of Lancaster, the high God, has proclaimed him full of knighthood and all grace.
sentences.zh: 兰开斯特的亨利，至高的上帝，已宣告他充满骑士精神和一切恩典。

sentences.en: So you can imagine that, you know, slightly annoying Richard II.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，这会让理查德二世感到有点恼火。

sentences.en: Richard, as we discussed before, is a man of great sensitivity, but also one of great vindictiveness.
sentences.zh: 理查德，正如我们之前讨论过的，是一个非常敏感，但也非常记仇的人。

sentences.en: And kind of, he's a hater, isn't he, Richard?
sentences.zh: 而且，他是个“黑粉”，不是吗，理查德？

sentences.en: He is a hater.
sentences.zh: 他确实是个“黑粉”。

sentences.en: And he feels resentment of his cousin's tremendous exploits and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 他对堂兄的巨大成就以及所有这些事情感到愤恨。

sentences.en: Which presumably for any king would show you up, right?
sentences.zh: 这对任何国王来说，大概都会让你相形见绌，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you're not a martial man and you're anxious that you're not seen in the same light.
sentences.zh: 因为你不是一个尚武的人，而且你担心自己不会被以同样的眼光看待。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I mean, people who heard our episode on the Hundred Years' War, Edward III,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听过我们关于百年战争那一集的朋友，爱德华三世，

sentences.en: the reason Edward III is seen as a great king is because he's very good at all the things that the nobility love.
sentences.zh: 爱德华三世之所以被视为伟大的国王，是因为他非常擅长贵族们所喜爱的一切事物。

sentences.en: So fighting, tournaments, all that kind of stuff, which Henry is as well.
sentences.zh: 比如战斗、锦标赛等等，亨利也同样擅长这些。

sentences.en: And Richard simply isn't.
sentences.zh: 而理查德根本不擅长。

sentences.en: And so it's unsurprising that towards the end of his reign, Richard really starts to try and kind of downgrade Henry to try and bump him off the line of succession.
sentences.zh: 所以毫不奇怪，在他统治末期，理查德真的开始试图贬低亨利，试图把他踢出继承顺序。

sentences.en: So in 1386, he announces that his heir is Roger Mortimer, so the son of Philippa, the daughter of Lionel.
sentences.zh: 所以在1386年，他宣布他的继承人是罗杰·莫蒂默，也就是莱昂内尔的女儿菲利帕的儿子。

sentences.en: So that is to mess up the line of succession that Edward III had decreed.
sentences.zh: 这打乱了爱德华三世所规定的继承顺序。

sentences.en: So Roger is then killed in Ireland in 1398 and he leaves a seven-year-old son, Edmund.
sentences.zh: 罗杰后来于1398年在爱尔兰被杀，留下了一个七岁的儿子埃德蒙。

sentences.en: So the question now is, is Edmund Richard II's heir or is John of Gaunt and Henry?
sentences.zh: 所以现在的问题是，埃德蒙是理查德二世的继承人，还是冈特的约翰和亨利？

sentences.en: It's kind of up for grabs.
sentences.zh: 这有点悬而未决。

sentences.en: But just to make absolutely certain that it's going to be the young Edmund, Richard then in 1398 exiles Henry for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 但为了确保一定是年轻的埃德蒙，理查德在1398年将亨利流放了10年。

sentences.en: And the following year when John of Gaunt dies, the question then is,
sentences.zh: 第二年，当冈特的约翰去世时，问题就来了，

sentences.en: will the exiled Henry be allowed to come back and take over his lands and inherit John of Gaunt's title of Duke of Lancaster?
sentences.zh: 被流放的亨利是否会被允许回来接管他的土地，并继承冈特的约翰的兰开斯特公爵头衔？

sentences.en: And Richard says, no, he's going to take over all of Henry's lands.
sentences.zh: 理查德说不，他要接管亨利所有的土地。

sentences.en: And he doesn't award the stewardship of England, which has been held by the House of Lancaster for a century to Henry.
sentences.zh: 而且他没有把由兰开斯特家族持有一个世纪的英格兰管家职位授予亨利。

sentences.en: And basically he strips him of everything.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他剥夺了他的一切。

sentences.en: And it's this that precipitates Henry's return from exile.
sentences.zh: 正是这一点促使亨利从流放中归来。

sentences.en: He lands at Ravenspur just down the Humber from Hull.
sentences.zh: 他在赫尔附近的雷文斯普尔登陆。

sentences.en: And within a few months, Richard has been abandoned by his men.
sentences.zh: 几个月内，理查德就被他的人抛弃了。

sentences.en: He's been captured.
sentences.zh: 他被俘虏了。

sentences.en: He's been deposed.
sentences.zh: 他被废黜了。

sentences.en: And he ends up being killed.
sentences.zh: 他最终被杀。

sentences.en: And Henry obviously does this for personal reasons.
sentences.zh: 亨利显然是出于个人原因才这么做的。

sentences.en: When he lands, he says, I'm coming back to reclaim my lands.
sentences.zh: 当他登陆时，他说，我回来是为了收回我的土地。

sentences.en: I'm doing it to uphold the laws of succession.
sentences.zh: 我这样做是为了维护继承法。

sentences.en: And this is widely accepted because what Richard has done, it's not just an attack on Henry himself,
sentences.zh: 这一点被广泛接受，因为理查德所做的，不仅是对亨利本人的攻击，

sentences.en: but on the entire basis of succession that underpins the way that England is organized.
sentences.zh: 而且是对支撑英格兰组织方式的整个继承基础的攻击。

sentences.en: So all the nobility, when they see what Richard has done, is thinking, well, this could happen to us.
sentences.zh: 所以所有的贵族，当他们看到理查德所做的事情时，都在想，这事儿也可能发生在我们身上。

sentences.en: This is terrifying.
sentences.zh: 这太可怕了。

sentences.en: So when Henry takes over, I mean, Tom, you always like to make this point about an anointed king.
sentences.zh: 所以当亨利接管政权时，汤姆，你总是喜欢强调受膏国王这一点。

sentences.en: You know, it's very special.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这非常特殊。

sentences.en: It's a terrible thing to topple an anointed king, all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 推翻一位受膏国王是一件可怕的事情，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And Shakespeare plays with that in Henry IV, Parts I and II.
sentences.zh: 莎士比亚在《亨利四世》第一部和第二部中探讨了这一点。

sentences.en: But do you think that among the elite, people think Henry's in a very difficult position, of course, but he's probably done the right thing.
sentences.zh: 但你认为在精英阶层中，人们是否认为亨利处于一个非常困难的境地，当然，但他可能做了正确的事。

sentences.en: Richard had to go.
sentences.zh: 理查德必须走。

sentences.en: We don't like it, maybe, but we just have to live with it.
sentences.zh: 我们可能不喜欢这样，但我们只能接受。

sentences.en: Yes, I mean, most of them do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，他们大多数人都是这么想的。

sentences.en: Most of the nobility swing behind him.
sentences.zh: 大多数贵族都倒向了他。

sentences.en: As I said, they're worried that, you know, they don't want their own lands being confiscated.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，他们担心，你知道，他们不想自己的土地被没收。

sentences.en: Yeah, Richard's out of control.
sentences.zh: 是的，理查德失控了。

sentences.en: They feel that Richard is essentially instituting a tyranny, a despotism.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得理查德本质上是在建立一种暴政，一种专制。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the family that particularly swing behind Henry are the Perses, who are the great power in the north, in Northumberland,
sentences.zh: 特别倒向亨利的家族是珀西家族，他们是北方诺森伯兰的强大势力，

sentences.en: the guardians of the northern marches against the Scots.
sentences.zh: 是抵御苏格兰人的北方边境守护者。

sentences.en: But there's also a sense in which Henry is reaching out beyond the nobility to the people.
sentences.zh: 但某种程度上，亨利也在超越贵族，向民众伸出援手。

sentences.en: And when he becomes king, he does it not by right of succession, but by election.
sentences.zh: 当他成为国王时，他不是靠继承权，而是靠选举。

sentences.en: So there's a sense almost that he is, I mean,
sentences.zh: 所以几乎有一种感觉，他就是，我的意思是，

sentences.en: I think that the closest that you get in the whole of medieval English history to a prime minister coming in and replacing a kind of clapped out administration.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是整个中世纪英国历史上最接近于一位首相上台并取代一个破败政府的情况。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The sense of election that Henry has been chosen is really, really important.
sentences.zh: 亨利是被选出来的这种选举感非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: And that's why Henry, unlike any other English king, really has to work hard on the propaganda to kind of justify how and why he's become king.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么亨利，不像其他任何英国国王，必须在宣传上下大功夫，来证明他如何以及为何成为国王。

sentences.en: You know, he pulls out all the stops.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他竭尽全力。

sentences.en: He promulgates prophecies by Merlin that he's going to be a great king.
sentences.zh: 他颁布了梅林的预言，说他将成为一位伟大的国王。

sentences.en: There's a tremendous story that is told by a Welsh priest called Adam of Aske, who we'll be meeting throughout the story,
sentences.zh: 有一个非常精彩的故事，是由一位叫亚当·阿斯克的威尔士牧师讲述的，我们会在整个故事中遇到他，

sentences.en: who says that there was a greyhound who was a bit like the octopus in the World Cup.
sentences.zh: 他说有一只灰狗，有点像世界杯里的那只章鱼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, you can kind of choose winners.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以选择赢家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This greyhound had abandoned a duke who was about to die, goes to Richard.
sentences.zh: 这只灰狗抛弃了一位即将死去的公爵，走向了理查德。

sentences.en: And then when Henry comes, the greyhound abandons Richard and goes to Henry, you know, absolutely gazed up at him with great big brown eyes full of love.
sentences.zh: 然后当亨利来的时候，灰狗抛弃了理查德，走向了亨利，你知道，用充满爱意的大棕眼睛凝视着他。

sentences.en: And then subsequently, when Henry meets Richard, the greyhound completely ignores Richard, can't even remember him.
sentences.zh: 随后，当亨利见到理查德时，灰狗完全无视了理查德，甚至记不起他了。

sentences.en: And this is an infallible proof that Henry has been chosen to be king.
sentences.zh: 这是亨利被选为国王的绝对证据。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that story sounds like it's definitely true, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 那个故事听起来绝对是真的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是。

sentences.en: Who would question that?
sentences.zh: 谁会质疑呢？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是。

sentences.en: But I mean, it's definitely the case that when, so Henry ends up capturing Richard, they process into London.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，当亨利最终俘虏理查德时，他们进入伦敦，这绝对是事实。

sentences.en: Henry is cheered.
sentences.zh: 亨利受到了欢呼。

sentences.en: He's greeted as a kind of conquering hero.
sentences.zh: 他被当作一位征服英雄来迎接。

sentences.en: And when he's elected king, he plays it very, very well.
sentences.zh: 当他被选为国王时，他表现得非常、非常好。

sentences.en: And he rises from his seat and he makes the sign of the cross and he commends himself to God.
sentences.zh: 他从座位上站起来，画了一个十字，并把自己托付给上帝。

sentences.en: And he delivers his claim, not in French, not in Latin, but in English.
sentences.zh: 他发表了他的声明，不是用法语，不是用拉丁语，而是用英语。

sentences.en: And Chris Given Wilson, in his biography, says, you know, this is the first declaration by a king in the English tongue.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·吉文·威尔逊在他的传记中说，你知道，这是国王第一次用英语发表声明。

sentences.en: It's the equivalent of the prime minister standing outside Downing Street and making his first address to the nation.
sentences.zh: 这相当于首相站在唐宁街外向全国发表第一次演讲。

sentences.en: But doing it in English is sending a message that he's not going to be as remote and as autocratic and as Frenchified as Richard.
sentences.zh: 但用英语这样做是在传递一个信息，即他不会像理查德那样疏远、专制和法国化。

sentences.en: Is he?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Is that what it's basically saying?
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: I think it is, but I think it's also saying, you know, that he is the people's king.
sentences.zh: 我认为是这样，但我认为这也意味着，你知道，他是人民的国王。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because this matters in a way that it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 因为这很重要，以一种以前的方式。

sentences.en: It hadn't for any previous king because in a way, public enthusiasm for him, both among the nobility, but also among the great mass of the English people,
sentences.zh: 这对任何以前的国王来说都不重要，因为在某种程度上，公众对他的热情，无论是在贵族中，还是在广大英国民众中，

sentences.en: is the key to his legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 是他合法性的关键。

sentences.en: It's the only source of legitimacy that he has because he can't rely on the rules of succession because there's this problem that there's this eight-year-old Edmund,
sentences.zh: 这是他拥有的唯一合法性来源，因为他不能依赖继承规则，因为存在那个八岁的埃德蒙的问题，

sentences.en: under the son of Roger, the Earl of March, you know, I mean, he's lurking around.
sentences.zh: 也就是马奇伯爵罗杰的儿子，你知道，我的意思是，他潜伏在周围。

sentences.en: And so Henry grabs him and puts him in a kind of silken imprisonment in Windsor.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利抓住了他，把他关进了温莎城堡，进行某种丝绸般的监禁。

sentences.en: You know, but he can't harp on his right to the succession.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但他不能总是强调他的继承权。

sentences.en: So it has to be about election.
sentences.zh: 所以这必须与选举有关。

sentences.en: And of course, the other thing that it requires him to do is really, really go in hard condemning Richard as a kind of tyrant.
sentences.zh: 当然，他还需要做的另一件事是，必须非常、非常强硬地谴责理查德，将其定性为某种暴君。

sentences.en: And so when he becomes king, again, very like a kind of prime minister,
sentences.zh: 所以当他成为国王时，同样地，就像某种首相一样，

sentences.en: he makes it absolutely clear and he makes it a public proclamation that he's going to respect property rights and he's going to respect the will of the people.
sentences.zh: 他明确表示并公开宣布，他将尊重财产权，尊重人民的意愿。

sentences.en: So in a sense, you know, as king, he is the servant of the people.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，你知道，作为国王，他是人民的公仆。

sentences.en: And this is a very, very novel tone.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常、非常新颖的基调。

sentences.en: You haven't had this before.
sentences.zh: 以前从未有过这种情况。

sentences.en: I mean, you're still doing a great job of selling him to the listeners, I would imagine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想你还是成功地向听众推销了他。

sentences.en: Well, he's in an incredibly invidious position because, you know, this isn't the kind of thing that a king should have to do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他处于一个极其令人反感的境地，因为你知道，这不是国王应该做的事情。

sentences.en: A king ascends by right.
sentences.zh: 国王是凭权利登基的。

sentences.en: Do you know what, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: In a way, I mean, a lot of people will bridle at this comparison, but we did a podcast about the princes in the tower.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我的意思是，很多人会对这种比较感到反感，但我们做过一期关于塔中王子的播客。

sentences.en: Richard III was in a really tough position then and he had to kill his nephews.
sentences.zh: 理查三世当时处境非常艰难，他不得不杀掉他的侄子们。

sentences.en: And you know that some people associated with this podcast commend him for that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一些与本播客相关的人还称赞他这样做。

sentences.en: But Henry IV was in a similarly difficult position.
sentences.zh: 但亨利四世也处于同样困难的境地。

sentences.en: He was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It was like win or buSt.
sentences.zh: 这就像是孤注一掷。

sentences.en: If he didn't topple Richard and basically kill him and take the throne, then he might as well go and live in a hut back in the Baltic or something.
sentences.zh: 如果他不推翻理查德，不杀了他并夺取王位，那么他不如回到波罗的海那边去住茅屋算了。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: And I think that had Henry been toppled, he would be remembered as a kind of Richard III.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果亨利被推翻，他会被人们记住为某种理查三世式的人物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Not just a usurper, but a failure.
sentences.zh: 不仅是一个篡位者，还是一个失败者。

sentences.en: Yeah, I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: He would have been regarded as a failure.
sentences.zh: 他会被视为一个失败者。

sentences.en: But of course, he isn't a failure.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他并不是一个失败者。

sentences.en: The only thing is, he's promising this great new start.
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是，他承诺了一个伟大的新开端。

sentences.en: But as we know with any incoming prime minister, to use your analogy, there's no such thing really as a clean break, is there?
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所知，对于任何新上任的首相，用你的类比来说，实际上并没有所谓的彻底决裂，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, is he wrestling with the same problems that Richard was, basically?
sentences.zh: 那么，他基本上是在应对理查德曾经面临的同样问题吗？

sentences.en: He is, but there are also advantages to this.
sentences.zh: 是的，但这样做也有优势。

sentences.en: So, again, for comparison with the prime minister, one of the things that is working to Henry's advantage is the fact that by this stage,
sentences.zh: 所以，再次与首相进行比较，亨利的一个优势在于，到了这个阶段，

sentences.en: England is basically the most centralised kingdom in Europe, meaning in turn that it's the most manageable.
sentences.zh: 英格兰基本上是欧洲最中央集权的王国，这意味着它也是最易于管理的。

sentences.en: And so, you effectively have a kind of cadre of civil servants who are working in offices that are based in Westminster, the chancery, the exchequer,
sentences.zh: 因此，你实际上拥有了一批公务员，他们在威斯敏斯特、大法官法庭、财政部等机构办公，

sentences.en: these frameworks of government that government today has essentially inherited from this period.
sentences.zh: 这些政府框架本质上是当今政府从那个时期继承下来的。

sentences.en: And so, as a result, despite all the convulsions, the toppling of Richard II, the coming to power of Henry IV, government goes on, as it does today.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管经历了所有的动荡，理查二世的倒台，亨利四世的上台，政府依然在运作，就像今天一样。

sentences.en: You know, one government falls, another government comes in, but the civil service continues.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一届政府倒台，另一届政府上台，但公务员制度依然延续。

sentences.en: So, that's a positive.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个积极因素。

sentences.en: But as you say, there is also, he's essentially inherited the problems that Richard II was facing.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，他本质上也继承了理查二世所面临的问题。

sentences.en: You know, how do you deal with financial shortfall?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你如何处理财政赤字？

sentences.en: Richard II had burned through money.
sentences.zh: 理查二世挥霍无度。

sentences.en: Parliament was very reluctant to vote him money.
sentences.zh: 议会非常不情愿给他拨款。

sentences.en: And Henry IV has the problem that people believe that he has promised there will be no more tax rises.
sentences.zh: 而亨利四世面临的问题是，人们认为他承诺过不会再加税。

sentences.en: So, I mean, again, very familiar.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这又非常熟悉了。

sentences.en: This is always the way with incoming prime ministers.
sentences.zh: 新上任的首相总是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, he's seen as having made, as part of his pitch, that there will be no tax rises.
sentences.zh: 所以，他被视为在他的竞选纲领中承诺过不会加税。

sentences.en: And, in fact, you know, shortly after he's crowned, in Somerset, there's a tax collector who's beaten to death because, and I'll quote,
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道，在他加冕后不久，在萨默塞特郡，一名税务官被殴打致死，因为——我引用一下——

sentences.en: his demands were contrary to the promise excusing them from such payments which the king had made to them at the time of his happy return.
sentences.zh: 他的要求违背了国王在幸福回归时向他们做出的免除此类付款的承诺。

sentences.en: So, people across England are saying, brilliant, we've got this new king.
sentences.zh: 所以，全英格兰的人都在说，太棒了，我们有了这位新国王。

sentences.en: We don't have to pay taxes.
sentences.zh: 我们不用交税了。

sentences.en: It's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: You know, but this is a real problem for Henry because he really needs money.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但这对亨利来说是个真正的问题，因为他确实需要钱。

sentences.en: I mean, he's the king now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他现在是国王了。

sentences.en: There's also the problem that he needs to keep the Perses in particular on board.
sentences.zh: 还有一个问题是，他需要特别争取珀西家族的支持。

sentences.en: If he loses them, he's in real trouble.
sentences.zh: 如果他失去了他们，他就会陷入真正的麻烦。

sentences.en: And there's also the fact that England is surrounded by enemies.
sentences.zh: 而且还有一个事实是，英格兰被敌人包围了。

sentences.en: So, officially, still at war with France, but there are also enemies actually on the island of Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以，官方上，仍然与法国处于战争状态，但实际上在不列颠岛上也有敌人。

sentences.en: So, there are the Scots, the weasel Scot, as Shakespeare describes them in Henry V, always sniffing out, you know, trouble in England.
sentences.zh: 所以，有苏格兰人，正如莎士比亚在《亨利五世》中所描述的那样，那些狡猾的苏格兰人，总是嗅探着英格兰的麻烦。

sentences.en: And there's also hints of kind of trouble in Wales, which has been under English rule for a century.
sentences.zh: 而且还有威尔士出现麻烦的迹象，那里已经被英国统治了一个世纪。

sentences.en: So, these are all probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些都是问题。

sentences.en: But I think the biggest problem, which we've already kind of hinted at, is that having come to power as a usurper, Henry then has to rule as a regicide.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最大的问题，我们已经暗示过了，那就是作为篡位者上台后，亨利必须以弑君者的身份进行统治。

sentences.en: Because, with the deposition of Richard II, he's bundled him off to one of the great Lancastrian castles, Pontefract, and wants to just basically leave him there.
sentences.zh: 因为，随着理查二世的被废黜，他把他关进了兰开斯特家族最伟大的城堡之一——庞特弗拉克特城堡，并想基本上就把他留在那里。

sentences.en: But there are conspiracies.
sentences.zh: 但阴谋不断。

sentences.en: There are people trying to overthrow Henry, bring back Richard II.
sentences.zh: 有人试图推翻亨利，带回理查二世。

sentences.en: And there's one in particular.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个特别的阴谋。

sentences.en: It's called the Epiphany Rising, because it happens in the season of Epiphany.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“主显节起义”，因为它发生在主显节期间。

sentences.en: And Henry treats this very, very brutally.
sentences.zh: 亨利对此处理得非常、非常残酷。

sentences.en: Even though he has a reputation for clemency, you know, he can't afford to show any mercy here.
sentences.zh: 尽管他以仁慈著称，你知道，他在这里可不敢表现出任何怜悯。

sentences.en: So, our friend Adam of Ask, the Welsh chaplain, he describes that he was in London at the time, after the execution of all the conspirators in this.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的朋友，威尔士牧师阿斯克的亚当，他描述说当时他在伦敦，在所有阴谋者被处决之后。

sentences.en: And he describes seeing that their bodies being carried through London, chopped up like the carcasses of beasts killed in the chase,
sentences.zh: 他描述看到他们的尸体被运过伦敦，像猎杀的野兽尸体一样被剁碎，

sentences.en: partly in sacks and partly on poles slung across pairs of men's shoulders.
sentences.zh: 有的装在麻袋里，有的挂在横跨在两人肩上的杆子上。

sentences.en: That's sending a message, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那是在传递一个信息，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well, sending a message, but essentially sending a message that his regime is pretty unstable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是在传递信息，但本质上是在传递一个信息，即他的政权相当不稳定。

sentences.en: And so, the question is, as a usurper and a regicide, how is Henry going to cope with all the challenges that are clearly coming his way?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，作为一个篡位者和弑君者，亨利将如何应对显然即将到来的所有挑战？

sentences.en: And just before we go to the break, one quick question.
sentences.zh: 在休息之前，先问一个简短的问题。

sentences.en: If I met Henry IV at this point, what's he like?
sentences.zh: 如果我现在见到亨利四世，他是什么样的人？

sentences.en: I mean, you've said he's very glamorous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你说他非常有魅力。

sentences.en: He's obviously very brave.
sentences.zh: 他显然非常勇敢。

sentences.en: He's a bit of an alpha male because of all the tournaments and the crusades and stuff.
sentences.zh: 因为所有的锦标赛、十字军东征之类的活动，他有点像个阿尔法男。

sentences.en: But you then said a reputation for clemency.
sentences.zh: 但你随后又说他以仁慈著称。

sentences.en: So, he's a man that other people admire?
sentences.zh: 所以，他是一个受人敬仰的人吗？

sentences.en: He is a man who other people admire, yes.
sentences.zh: 他确实是一个受人敬仰的人，是的。

sentences.en: He's also very literate.
sentences.zh: 他非常有文化。

sentences.en: He's very smart.
sentences.zh: 他非常聪明。

sentences.en: He's deeply Christian.
sentences.zh: 他是一位虔诚的基督徒。

sentences.en: He thinks very profoundly about his faith.
sentences.zh: 他对自己信仰的思考非常深刻。

sentences.en: So, in all kinds of ways, he's admirable.
sentences.zh: 所以，在各方面，他都是令人钦佩的。

sentences.en: But I think his tragedy is that all these qualities, which had helped to bring him to the throne,
sentences.zh: 但我认为他的悲剧在于，所有这些曾经帮助他登上王位的品质，

sentences.en: after he's come to the throne and after he's been responsible for the murder of Richard II, people don't believe them anymore.
sentences.zh: 在他登上王位并对理查二世的谋杀负责之后，人们不再相信这些品质了。

sentences.en: And he's in a desperate struggle to stop the entire situation, as we will see, from collapsing.
sentences.zh: 他正处于一场绝望的斗争中，正如我们将看到的，试图阻止整个局势崩溃。

sentences.en: What a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 真是个悬念。

sentences.en: So, come back after the break to see if he can stave off disaster.
sentences.zh: 所以，休息后回来看看他能否避免灾难。

sentences.zh: 那次航班，载有350名乘客。

sentences.zh: 大博弈。

sentences.zh: 英国和俄罗斯之间的战略斗争。

sentences.zh: 我们评估，呃，首相。

sentences.zh: 有高度把握，这是俄罗斯所为。

sentences.zh: 让俄罗斯人承担责任就是第三次世界大战。

sentences.zh: 他们击落了一架载有350人的英国客机。

sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫的那个人在玩弄权术，亚历克斯。

sentences.zh: 你必须问问自己，你想玩还是不想玩？

sentences.zh: 你是首相。

sentences.zh: 你什么都没做！

sentences.zh: 我们需要了解政策背景。

sentences.zh: 今天所有相关的背景都将构建为一个框架。

sentences.en: And disseminated into an operation order.
sentences.zh: 并分发成一份作战命令。

sentences.en: Or Frago.
sentences.zh: 或者碎片化命令。

sentences.en: Or Frago that says to kill the President of Russia.
sentences.zh: 或者一份要求刺杀俄罗斯总统的碎片化命令。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 来自Gullhanger的新闻。

sentences.zh: 谁能完成这个任务？
