sentences.zh: 而威尔士就在柴郡旁边。

sentences.en: And Wales, in the autumn of 1400, erupts into rebellion in a way that, I mean, is really startling.
sentences.zh: 1400年秋天，威尔士爆发了叛乱，其方式真的令人震惊。

sentences.en: Because as we said, Wales has been conquered for a century, subdued by Edward I, who'd built a chain of great castles across the northern reaches of the principality,
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们所说，威尔士已经被征服了一个世纪，被爱德华一世镇压，他在公国北部边缘建造了一连串伟大的城堡，

sentences.en: had named his son, the future Edward II, Prince of Wales.
sentences.zh: 并命名他的儿子，未来的爱德华二世为威尔士亲王。

sentences.en: And that's, you know, a title that Prince Henry has now succeeded Prince Hal.
sentences.zh: 而那个头衔，你知道，现在亨利王子已经接替了哈尔王子。

sentences.en: But on the 16th of September, 1400, even before the prince has arrived in Cheshire, another man, a Welshman, has laid claim to the title of Prince of Wales.
sentences.zh: 但在1400年9月16日，甚至在王子到达柴郡之前，另一个人，一个威尔士人，已经宣称拥有威尔士亲王的头衔。

sentences.en: And this is a man called Owen Glyndour.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫欧文·格林道尔。

sentences.en: And he is a man who has the blood of Welsh princes in his veins.
sentences.zh: 他是一个血管里流淌着威尔士亲王血统的人。

sentences.en: So Rhys Davies, who's the great historian of late medieval Wales and has written a brilliant book on Glyndour's rebellion,
sentences.zh: 所以里斯·戴维斯，那位研究中世纪晚期威尔士的伟大历史学家，曾写过一本关于格林道尔叛乱的精彩著作，

sentences.en: he writes, nobody needed to flatter or lie in the recital of Owen's genealogy.
sentences.zh: 他写道，在叙述欧文的家谱时，没人需要奉承或撒谎。

sentences.en: It was the finest in Wales.
sentences.zh: 那是威尔士最高贵的血统。

sentences.en: Yeah, the finest blood in Wales, Tom.
sentences.zh: 没错，威尔士最高贵的血统，汤姆。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: He has the blood of the two great princely lions in his veins.
sentences.zh: 他的血管里流淌着两位伟大亲王雄狮的血液。

sentences.en: So, you know, great subject for bardic song, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是吟游诗人歌曲的绝佳题材，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: And I think it's fair to say that Owen Glyndour is a great man for a bardic song.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以说，欧文·格林道尔确实是吟游诗人歌曲的绝佳素材。

sentences.en: Well, the trouble is that the English, and some people would say this is a theme of Anglo-Welsh history,
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题在于英国人——有些人会说这是英威尔历史的一个主题——

sentences.en: the English don't treat him with the seriousness that he thinks he deserves.
sentences.zh: 英国人并没有以他认为应有的严肃态度对待他。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 没错，是这样吧？

sentences.en: No, because, as I say, Wales has been conquered for a century.
sentences.zh: 不，因为正如我所说，威尔士已经被征服了一个世纪。

sentences.en: I mean, he may have the blood of princes in his veins, but he's still only a kind of member of the minor gentry.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他可能血管里流着亲王的血，但他终究只是个小乡绅。

sentences.en: It's absolutely ridiculous that this upstart should think to challenge the authentic Prince of Wales and the might of the English king.
sentences.zh: 这个暴发户竟然想挑战正统的威尔士亲王和英格兰国王的威严，这简直太荒谬了。

sentences.en: So they do see it as kind of basically a bit ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实认为这基本上有点荒谬。

sentences.en: And I think that reflects the fact that Wales at this point is kind of halfway house.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了威尔士在这一点上处于一种中间状态的事实。

sentences.en: I mean, it is still Welsh, but it has been anglicized pretty strongly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它仍然是威尔士的，但已经被相当强烈地英格兰化了。

sentences.en: And you can see this in the figure of Owen himself.
sentences.zh: 你可以从欧文本人身上看出这一点。

sentences.en: So in lots of ways, he's quite assimilated.
sentences.zh: 所以在很多方面，他已经相当同化了。

sentences.en: He's trained as a lawyer in London.
sentences.zh: 他在伦敦接受过律师培训。

sentences.en: He's served in the garrison at Berwick-upon-Tweed.
sentences.zh: 他曾在特威德河畔贝里克驻军服役。

sentences.en: His wife is of English descent.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子是英格兰裔。

sentences.en: But he is also full of seething resentments, which are entirely legitimate.
sentences.zh: 但他内心也充满了强烈的愤懑，而这些愤懑完全是合情合理的。

sentences.en: Because Wales is subject to laws that were instituted by Edward I that have basically imposed a form of apartheid on the principality.
sentences.zh: 因为威尔士受制于爱德华一世制定的法律，这些法律基本上在威尔士公国实行了一种种族隔离制度。

sentences.en: The Welsh are legally penalized in all kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 威尔士人在法律上受到各种形式的惩罚。

sentences.en: They're stopped from wielding power.
sentences.zh: 他们被禁止掌握权力。

sentences.en: Their economic opportunities are very much inhibited by the economic rights that are given to English settlers.
sentences.zh: 他们的经济机会受到英格兰定居者所享有的经济权利的极大限制。

sentences.en: And I think that these have always been resented by the Welsh aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 我认为威尔士贵族一直对此心怀不满。

sentences.en: And you might say, Dominic, that the kindling is in place and that Owen's claim to be the Prince of Wales is the striking of the match.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，多米尼克，干柴已经备好，而欧文自称威尔士亲王，就是划下那根火柴的动作。

sentences.en: But it's not the spark that he has a row with his neighbor.
sentences.zh: 但他与邻居发生争执并非导火索。

sentences.en: Lord Ruthen, Reginald Grey.
sentences.zh: 鲁辛勋爵，雷金纳德·格雷。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's always the way that it's your neighbors are the people you really have to fear.
sentences.zh: 人们真正需要提防的往往就是自己的邻居，向来如此。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they've basically been, they hate each other.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上就是互相憎恨。

sentences.en: They've been kind of quarreling over, you know, ditches.
sentences.zh: 他们一直为了，你知道，一些沟渠之类的小事争吵不休。

sentences.en: Harking about a fence.
sentences.zh: 为了篱笆的事喋喋不休。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Cows wandering into each other's lands and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 牛群闯入对方的土地等等诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And basically, Owen has this blazing row with Lord Ruthen.
sentences.zh: 基本上，欧文与鲁辛勋爵爆发了激烈的争吵。

sentences.en: And it's this that prompts him to go storming off and saying that he's the Prince of Wales, which is obviously a brilliant way of upstaging his near neighbor.
sentences.zh: 正是这件事促使他愤然离去，并宣称自己是威尔士亲王，这显然是压过他那位近邻的绝妙手段。

sentences.en: But there is no question that in doing that, you know, this argument over, you know, who's building the fence on the lower field,
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，在做这件事的时候，你知道，这场关于，你知道，谁在下层田地建篱笆的争论，

sentences.en: it explodes because there is this incredible Welsh sense of nationalist resentment.
sentences.zh: 之所以会爆发，是因为威尔士人心中有着一种难以置信的民族主义愤懑。

sentences.en: And the moment he's made this announcement, it's not just his own feudal followers, but people from across northern Wales who kind of flock to his banner.
sentences.zh: 就在他宣布这一消息的那一刻，不仅是他自己的封建追随者，连威尔士北部各地的人们也纷纷投奔他的旗帜。

sentences.en: And they just go on the rampage.
sentences.zh: 他们开始横冲直撞。

sentences.en: They kind of go sweeping off.
sentences.zh: 他们开始横扫一切。

sentences.en: They burn all Ruthen's fields.
sentences.zh: 他们烧毁了鲁辛所有的田地。

sentences.en: They go off and they attack all kinds of English settlements across northern Wales.
sentences.zh: 他们四处出击，袭击了威尔士北部各地的英格兰定居点。

sentences.en: And Rhys-Davis says from the beginning, Owen's crusade was anti-English.
sentences.zh: 里斯-戴维斯说，从一开始，欧文的十字军东征就是反英格兰的。

sentences.en: That this is a kind of proto-nationalist rebellion.
sentences.zh: 这是一场原始民族主义的叛乱。

sentences.en: And Henry, when he's informed of this, I mean, he takes it seriously, but not too seriously.
sentences.zh: 而亨利在得知此事时，我的意思是，他确实认真对待了，但并没有太当回事。

sentences.en: Because despite the fact that, you know, a lot of fields are being burnt, Owen Glyndaer and his followers are in no position to kind of capture castles,
sentences.zh: 因为尽管，你知道，很多田地被烧毁了，但欧文·格林多及其追随者根本没有能力攻占城堡，

sentences.en: to actually seize towns permanently.
sentences.zh: 无法真正长期占领城镇。

sentences.en: And seven days after he's proclaimed himself Prince of Wales, he's defeated in a skirmish.
sentences.zh: 在他自封为威尔士亲王七天后，他在一场小规模冲突中战败了。

sentences.en: So it looks like actually, you know, it's blazed up and it's going to die down again.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来，你知道，这只是火势燃起又会熄灭而已。

sentences.en: But then what happens is that in Anglesey, so the island off the northwest of Wales, another uprising is launched.
sentences.zh: 但随后发生的事情是，在安格尔西岛，也就是威尔士西北部的那个岛屿上，又爆发了另一场起义。

sentences.en: And this is launched by two brothers, Rhys and Gwilym Aptuda.
sentences.zh: 这次起义是由里斯和格威利姆·阿普图多两兄弟发起的。

sentences.en: It's a name to conjure with.
sentences.zh: 这名字真让人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Yeah, a name to conjure with.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实让人印象深刻。

sentences.en: So therefore you have these two kind of uprisings in Wales and they must surely have been coordinated.
sentences.zh: 所以，威尔士出现了这两场起义，它们肯定经过了协调。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I was going to ask about that.
sentences.zh: 我正想问这个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do we know whether they are writing to each other or sending messages, the Tudors and Glyndaer?
sentences.zh: 我们知道都铎家族和格林多之间是否有书信往来或互通消息吗？

sentences.en: We don't for sure, but I think so.
sentences.zh: 我们不能确定，但我认为是有的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think the consensus would be that, yes, this is a coordinated uprising.
sentences.zh: 我认为共识应该是，是的，这是一场协调一致的起义。

sentences.en: So in October of 1400, Henry marches into the north.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1400年10月，亨利向北方进军。

sentences.en: He goes all the way to Carnarfon on the coast of Wales, the northwest coast of Wales.
sentences.zh: 他一路到达了威尔士海岸，即威尔士西北海岸的卡纳封。

sentences.en: He boosts up the garrison of all these kind of castles that had been built by Edward I, the fetters that had been thrown over the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 他加强了所有这些由爱德华一世建造的城堡的驻军，这些城堡就是套在威尔士人脖子上的枷锁。

sentences.en: He executes various rebels that he's taken prisoner.
sentences.zh: 他处决了俘虏的几名叛军。

sentences.en: And the rebellion seems over.
sentences.zh: 叛乱似乎结束了。

sentences.en: But it isn't.
sentences.zh: 但并没有。

sentences.en: Because on the 1st of April, April Fool's Day of the following year, which is also Good Friday, the captain of Conway Castle, one of these great Edwardian castles.
sentences.zh: 因为在次年的4月1日，也就是愚人节，同时也是耶稣受难日，康威城堡的指挥官，这些伟大的爱德华式城堡之一的指挥官。

sentences.en: It's Good Friday, he goes off to a church service.
sentences.zh: 那天是耶稣受难日，他去参加教堂礼拜了。

sentences.en: He takes all but five of the garrison with him.
sentences.zh: 他带走了驻军，只留下了五个人。

sentences.en: So essentially, there's only a kind of skeleton staff.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，那里只有极少数的留守人员。

sentences.en: And while he's at church, Gwilym Tudor, who's still very much on the scene, he's got 40 men with him.
sentences.zh: 当他在教堂时，格威利姆·都铎，他依然活跃在现场，带着40个人。

sentences.en: They sneak their way into the castle and they seize control of it.
sentences.zh: 他们潜入城堡并夺取了控制权。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is an amazing stunt.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一次惊人的壮举。

sentences.en: It seems to have come from nowhere.
sentences.zh: 它似乎凭空出现。

sentences.en: And they managed to hold out for two months, even though both Hotspur and the prince, so Prince Hal and Hotspur working together, you know, they lay siege to it.
sentences.zh: 尽管霍特斯浦和王子，也就是哈尔王子和霍特斯浦联手围攻，他们还是成功坚守了两个月。

sentences.en: And it's only at the end of May that Gwilym Tudor negotiates a surrender.
sentences.zh: 直到五月底，格威利姆·都铎才谈判投降。

sentences.en: And the terms are that they have to hand over nine of their defenders who were predictably put to death very horribly.
sentences.zh: 条件是他们必须交出九名守军，这些人不出所料地被极其残忍地处死了。

sentences.en: But the rest of them march out.
sentences.zh: 但其余的人撤走了。

sentences.en: And it's just a tremendous propaganda coup.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一次巨大的宣传政变。

sentences.en: And it's talked of across Wales.
sentences.zh: 整个威尔士都在谈论这件事。

sentences.en: And so the impact of this on the Welsh is to make them think, brilliant, you know, we could have a crack at the English.
sentences.zh: 这对威尔士人的影响是让他们觉得，太棒了，你知道，我们可以试着挑战一下英格兰人。

sentences.en: This is the kind of the boldness, the daring that might actually enable us to throw off the English yoke.
sentences.zh: 这种胆识和勇气或许真的能让我们摆脱英格兰的枷锁。

sentences.en: And in England, it causes outrage.
sentences.zh: 而在英格兰，这引起了公愤。

sentences.en: And so in London, the parliament says, you know, we've got to come down hard on this.
sentences.zh: 因此在伦敦，议会说，你知道，我们必须严厉打击这一点。

sentences.en: And members of parliament in London, they force through all these very, very kind of retributive laws, the penal laws they're called.
sentences.zh: 伦敦的议会议员们强行通过了所有这些非常、非常具有报复性的法律，即所谓的刑法。

sentences.en: Which are explicitly anti-Welsh statutes and ordinances.
sentences.zh: 这些明确是反威尔士的法规和条例。

sentences.en: And Rhys Davies says, you know, they are utterly racist and also completely counterproductive.
sentences.zh: 里斯·戴维斯说，你知道，它们完全是种族主义的，而且完全适得其反。

sentences.en: Because that sense of a kind of certain commonality between the Welsh and the English, a sense that the Welsh are becoming English, that the English are becoming Welsh.
sentences.zh: 因为那种威尔士人和英格兰人之间某种共同点的感觉，那种威尔士人正在变得英格兰化，英格兰人正在变得威尔士化的感觉。

sentences.en: It tears it up.
sentences.zh: 它被撕碎了。

sentences.en: The two sides become completely polarised again.
sentences.zh: 双方再次完全两极分化。

sentences.en: So here's your classic example of a kind of proto-colonialist administration not winning hearts and minds.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是那种准殖民行政管理未能赢得民心的典型例子。

sentences.en: And, you know, such administrations win when they persuade the bulk of kind of non-aligned opinion to support them.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当这种政府能够说服大多数非结盟的舆论支持他们时，他们才能获胜。

sentences.en: But what the English have done here is driven them away.
sentences.zh: 但英格兰人在这里所做的却是把他们推开了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, to a degree, the English had succeeded in persuading the Welsh to, you know, assimilate.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在某种程度上，英格兰人确实成功地说服了威尔士人去，你知道，同化。

sentences.en: And Owen Glendower being a kind of example of that.
sentences.zh: 欧文·格林多就是一个例子。

sentences.en: But this just totally explodes that.
sentences.zh: 但这彻底摧毁了这一点。

sentences.en: And the rebellion escalates and escalates and escalates.
sentences.zh: 叛乱不断升级，不断升级，不断升级。

sentences.en: And it spreads from North Wales, which had always been the hotbed of Welsh resistance, down into the central Wales.
sentences.zh: 它从一直是威尔士抵抗运动温床的北威尔士蔓延到了威尔士中部。

sentences.en: And even, you know, there are kind of bushfires of rebellion in southern Wales.
sentences.zh: 甚至，你知道，在南威尔士也出现了叛乱的星星之火。

sentences.en: So Henry IV launches another invasion.
sentences.zh: 于是亨利四世发动了另一次入侵。

sentences.en: But the Welsh just kind of melt into the hills.
sentences.zh: 但威尔士人只是融入了山丘之中。

sentences.en: And the moment Henry IV is withdrawn, Glendower pops out again from his mountain fastnesses.
sentences.zh: 而亨利四世一撤军，格林多又从他的山中堡垒里冒了出来。

sentences.en: And this time he's got an absolutely brilliant banner.
sentences.zh: 这一次他有一面绝对精彩的旗帜。

sentences.en: And it's a golden dragon on a white field.
sentences.zh: 那是一面白色底色上的金龙旗。

sentences.en: So not a red dragon.
sentences.zh: 所以不是红龙。

sentences.en: No, apparently it's a golden dragon.
sentences.zh: 不，显然是金龙。

sentences.en: But there are lots of red dragons.
sentences.zh: 但红龙也很多。

sentences.en: I mean, basically there are dragons everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上到处都是龙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's all tremendous excitement.
sentences.zh: 这一切都令人无比兴奋。

sentences.en: And there are prophecies and, you know, more prophecies from Merlin.
sentences.zh: 而且还有预言，你知道，更多来自梅林的预言。

sentences.en: And it's all kicking off.
sentences.zh: 一切都开始了。

sentences.en: And the following year, there are two brilliant victories for Owen, for Glendower.
sentences.zh: 第二年，欧文，也就是格林多，取得了两次辉煌的胜利。

sentences.en: So in the first of them, he captures his old enemy, Reginald Grey, Lord Ruffin.
sentences.zh: 在第一次胜利中，他俘虏了他的老敌人，鲁辛勋爵雷金纳德·格雷。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Grey is kind of led away on a donkey, bound tightly with thongs, the chronicler says.
sentences.zh: 编年史家说，格雷被紧紧地捆绑着，骑着驴被带走了。

sentences.en: He's now bitterly regretting that boundary dispute that kicked the whole thing off.
sentences.zh: 他现在非常后悔那场引发这一切的边界纠纷。

sentences.en: Yeah, he really is.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实很后悔。

sentences.en: He should have just let them have the ditch.
sentences.zh: 他本该直接把那条沟渠让给他们的。

sentences.en: And then shortly after that, there's an even more extraordinary victory for the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 在那之后不久，威尔士人又取得了一场更加非凡的胜利。

sentences.en: And this happens at a place called Pilith, which is just inside Wales.
sentences.zh: 这发生在皮利斯，就在威尔士境内。

sentences.en: And I visited it, actually, a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我几周前刚去过那里。

sentences.en: I did a road trip from Rye to Aberystwyth.
sentences.zh: 我从莱伊开车去阿伯里斯特威斯。

sentences.en: And we stopped at this place.
sentences.zh: 我们在那个地方停了下来。

sentences.en: And it's a church on a hill.
sentences.zh: 那是一座山上的教堂。

sentences.en: And the Welsh had occupied it.
sentences.zh: 威尔士人占领了它。

sentences.en: And the guy who comes to attack them is Edmund Mortimer, who is the uncle of the younger Edmund.
sentences.zh: 来攻击他们的人是埃德蒙·莫蒂默，他是年轻埃德蒙的叔叔。

sentences.en: It's so confusing.
sentences.zh: 这太令人困惑了。

sentences.en: The younger Edmund Mortimer, who's the heir to the throne, who's stuck in Windsor.
sentences.zh: 年轻的埃德蒙·莫蒂默，他是王位继承人，被困在温莎。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's his uncle.
sentences.zh: 那是他的叔叔。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Another Edmund Mortimer.
sentences.zh: 另一个埃德蒙·莫蒂默。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's his uncle.
sentences.zh: 是的，是他的叔叔。

sentences.en: And he goes and attacks the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 他去攻击威尔士人。

sentences.en: And it's a very steep hill.
sentences.zh: 那是一座非常陡峭的山。

sentences.en: And it's a mad thing to do when you see it.
sentences.zh: 当你看到它时，会觉得那是一个疯狂的举动。

sentences.en: And he charges up a hill.
sentences.zh: 他冲上了一座山。

sentences.en: And his men get wiped out.
sentences.zh: 他的部下被全歼了。

sentences.en: And he gets captured.
sentences.zh: 他被俘虏了。

sentences.en: And English dead are left scattered all over the hillside.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人的尸体散落在山坡上。

sentences.en: And this features in the very opening of Henry IV, part one, where the description of the English dead, it's beastly, shameless transformation.
sentences.zh: 这在《亨利四世》第一部的开篇中有所体现，对英格兰人尸体的描述，那是一种野蛮、无耻的变形。

sentences.en: And what Shakespeare means by that is that they're all genitally mutilated.
sentences.zh: 莎士比亚的意思是他们都被阉割了。

sentences.en: The Welsh women, it is said, go out and just kind of hack off the genitals of the dead and dying English.
sentences.zh: 据说，威尔士妇女走出来，把那些死去的和垂死的英格兰人的生殖器割了下来。

sentences.en: Now, it has to be said that Rhys Davis says that this is just English propaganda.
sentences.zh: 现在必须说明的是，里斯·戴维斯说这只是英格兰人的宣传。

sentences.en: A number of English historians that I've read all say, yes, this happened.
sentences.zh: 我读过的一些英格兰历史学家都说，是的，这确实发生了。

sentences.en: So kind of interesting perspective, difference of perspective there.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种有趣的视角，视角的差异。

sentences.en: It wouldn't be unusual for it to happen, would it?
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种事也不足为奇，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I think back to the series we did about the American WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，回想一下我们做的关于美国西部的系列节目。

sentences.en: There was an awful lot of that kind of carry on there.
sentences.zh: 那里有很多那种行为。

sentences.en: I think the reason why Rhys Davis would say it was English propaganda is...
sentences.zh: 我想里斯·戴维斯之所以说这是英格兰人的宣传，是因为……

sentences.en: It's his Welsh.
sentences.zh: 因为他是威尔士人。

sentences.en: Well, no, it's the fact that this is not the kind of behavior that is expected of the defeated on a Christian battlefield.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不，是因为在基督教战场上，这并不是战败者应有的行为。

sentences.en: And it's casting the Welsh as sinister, pagan, barbarous savages.
sentences.zh: 而且这把威尔士人描绘成阴险、异教、野蛮的野蛮人。

sentences.en: So I'm not qualified to say whether it happened or not.
sentences.zh: 所以我没有资格说它是否发生过。

sentences.en: But certainly the English thought it.
sentences.zh: 但英格兰人确实是这么认为的。

sentences.en: I think this happens all the time in history.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种事在历史上经常发生。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, maybe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't think it's unusually Welsh.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不认为这是威尔士人特有的。

sentences.en: I just think it's standard conduct, actually.
sentences.zh: 我只是认为这实际上是标准行为。

sentences.en: I don't think it is.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: I don't think that after a battle, women come out and hack off testicles in medieval Europe, by and large.
sentences.zh: 我不认为在中世纪的欧洲，战斗结束后，妇女们会普遍出来割掉睾丸。

sentences.en: Dominic pulling a face.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克做了一个鬼脸。

sentences.en: Well, I think if they didn't...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得如果他们没这么做的话……

sentences.en: Because it causes a scandal.
sentences.zh: 因为这会引发丑闻。

sentences.en: If they didn't, I feel like they should have done.
sentences.zh: 如果他们没做，我觉得他们本该做的。

sentences.en: Anyway, let's continue.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们继续吧。

sentences.en: Okay, all right.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: So it's lots of bad blood in England because people are telling the story and believing it.
sentences.zh: 所以英格兰内部积怨很深，因为人们都在传述并相信这个故事。

sentences.en: And so Henry leads another expedition.
sentences.zh: 于是亨利又发动了一次远征。

sentences.en: And this one is even worse because it's an incredibly violent storm.
sentences.zh: 而这一次更糟糕，因为遇到了一场极其猛烈的风暴。

sentences.en: And it flattens the king's tent.
sentences.zh: 风暴把国王的帐篷都夷为平地了。

sentences.en: This great lightning bolt incinerates it.
sentences.zh: 一道巨大的闪电将其焚毁。

sentences.en: And Henry could very easily have died.
sentences.zh: 亨利当时很有可能就没命了。

sentences.en: And of course, everyone in Wales says that this has been conjured up by Glendower's magicians.
sentences.zh: 当然，威尔士的所有人都说这是格兰道尔的魔法师们召唤出来的。

sentences.en: So there's a general sense, this is great.
sentences.zh: 所以大家普遍觉得，这太棒了。

sentences.en: You know, we're hacking off testicles.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在割掉睾丸。

sentences.en: We've got storMs.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了风暴。

sentences.en: We've got dragons.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了龙。

sentences.en: It's absolutely brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这简直太精彩了。

sentences.en: Just on the magicians.
sentences.zh: 就说魔法师的事吧。

sentences.en: So magicians didn't play any part.
sentences.zh: 所以魔法师并没有参与其中。

sentences.en: You did a series about the Hundred Years' War, or the Third.
sentences.zh: 你做过关于百年战争，或者第三次战争的系列节目。

sentences.en: I don't recall any magicians in that series.
sentences.zh: 我不记得那个系列里有任何魔法师。

sentences.en: Do the English genuinely believe that the Welsh have magicians on their side?
sentences.zh: 英国人真的相信威尔士人有魔法师相助吗？

sentences.en: Kind of druid figures or something?
sentences.zh: 类似于德鲁伊那样的人物？

sentences.en: Because in Shakespeare's play, O England Hour is a kind of comedy magician, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为在莎士比亚的剧作里，欧文·格兰道尔是个滑稽的魔法师，不是吗？

sentences.en: Not exactly a comedy.
sentences.zh: 算不上滑稽。

sentences.en: Well, maybe that's just the productions I've seen generally play it for laughs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许只是我看到的那些制作通常把它演成了喜剧效果。

sentences.en: Hotspur laughs at him.
sentences.zh: 霍茨珀嘲笑他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But there's a sense that he's a very, actually, I mean, I think Shakespeare presents him as being very familiar.
sentences.zh: 但有一种感觉，实际上，我是说，我认为莎士比亚把他塑造成了一个非常熟悉的人。

sentences.en: He's called the great magician.
sentences.zh: 他被称为伟大的魔法师。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there is.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想确实有。

sentences.en: And I think that the English play it up as a way of showing, oh, the Welsh are just, you know, they're just savages.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为英国人夸大这一点是为了表明，哦，威尔士人不过是，你知道，他们只是野蛮人。

sentences.en: And the Welsh play it up because it's a way of intimidating the English.
sentences.zh: 而威尔士人夸大这一点是因为这是一种恐吓英国人的方式。

sentences.en: And also it's true to traditions that the English don't have.
sentences.zh: 而且这也符合英国人所不具备的传统。

sentences.en: So I think it's, you know, for all these reasons, the idea that Glendower has access to supernatural powers that, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，出于所有这些原因，格兰道尔能够获得超自然力量，而你知道，

sentences.en: the lumpen English in their plodding armor don't have is an important part of his image.
sentences.zh: 那些穿着笨重盔甲、步履蹒跚的英国人却无法企及，这是他形象中重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And, you know, Henry is for the moment powerless to do anything about it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，亨利目前对此无能为力。

sentences.en: His style of fighting is inadequate to cope with the kind of guerrilla warfare that England Dower is the master of.
sentences.zh: 他的战斗风格不足以应对格兰道尔所擅长的游击战。

sentences.en: But now he's facing trouble on another front, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但现在他在另一条战线上也面临麻烦，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it's not just the western border, but up north, in your neck of the woods, Tom, near your country estate.
sentences.zh: 因为不仅仅是西部边境，还有北方，汤姆，在你家附近，靠近你的乡村庄园。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's all kinds of ructions going on.
sentences.zh: 那里发生了各种各样的骚乱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, of course, because the Scots, you know, they're kept informed of what's going on in Wales and they think this is a perfect opportunity to launch a great raid on the north.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，因为苏格兰人，你知道，他们随时了解威尔士发生的事情，他们认为这是一个对北方发动大规模突袭的绝佳机会。

sentences.en: So this happens in September 1402 and it's led by the most formidable military figure in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 这件事发生在1402年9月，由苏格兰最强大的军事人物领导。

sentences.en: He's a guy called the Earl of Douglas.
sentences.zh: 他是一个叫道格拉斯伯爵的人。

sentences.en: And he leads his men across the Tweed and heads southwards down towards Newcastle, plundering and looting as he goes.
sentences.zh: 他带领手下越过特威德河，向南直奔纽卡斯尔，沿途烧杀抢掠。

sentences.en: And Hotspur, who's in Wales, is sent news.
sentences.zh: 而身在威尔士的霍茨珀收到了消息。

sentences.en: He goes galloping up using his Hotspurs to join his father and the two men meet up.
sentences.zh: 他骑着马飞奔而去，带着他的“热刺”们去与父亲会合，两人碰了头。

sentences.en: And although they are ready to oppose the Scots, it's clear that they are full of festering resentments against Henry.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们准备对抗苏格兰人，但很明显，他们对亨利充满了积怨。

sentences.en: So Hotspur is going not just to oppose Douglas, but to have a council of war with his father.
sentences.zh: 所以霍茨珀此行不仅是为了对抗道格拉斯，还要与父亲召开军事会议。

sentences.en: So Hotspur disagrees with Henry IV's strategy of fighting Owinglindar.
sentences.zh: 霍茨珀不同意亨利四世对抗欧文·格兰道尔的战略。

sentences.en: He thinks that there should be negotiations, an accommodation should be arrived at.
sentences.zh: 他认为应该进行谈判，达成某种妥协。

sentences.en: He feels that the Prince of Wales is stepping on his toes, that, you know, as Prince Hal gets older.
sentences.zh: 他觉得威尔士亲王正在越权，你知道，随着哈尔王子长大。

sentences.en: So he's starting to muscle in on a sphere of activity that Hotspur feels is his own.
sentences.zh: 他开始插手霍茨珀认为属于自己的活动领域。

sentences.en: And most incendiary of all, there is the fact that Edmund Mortimer, who is Hotspur's brother-in-law now,
sentences.zh: 最令人愤怒的是，埃德蒙·莫蒂默现在是霍茨珀的妹夫，

sentences.en: because Hotspur is married to Edmund Mortimer's sister, he's not being ransomed.
sentences.zh: 因为霍茨珀娶了埃德蒙·莫蒂默的妹妹，但他却没有被赎回。

sentences.en: Henry IV is refusing to ransom him and is refusing Edmund Mortimer the right to ransom himself.
sentences.zh: 亨利四世拒绝赎回他，也拒绝让埃德蒙·莫蒂默自赎。

sentences.en: And the reason for this, very obviously, is that the Mortimers are, you know, potential rivals.
sentences.zh: 而原因显而易见，莫蒂默家族是潜在的竞争对手。

sentences.en: So Henry, you know, actually having him captive by, you know, in Welsh hands is really good.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利，你知道，让他被威尔士人俘虏其实挺好的。

sentences.en: But Hotspur is very, very resentful of this.
sentences.zh: 但霍茨珀对此非常、非常怨恨。

sentences.en: And so he and his father consult.
sentences.zh: 于是他和父亲商量对策。

sentences.en: But before they can decide what to do about Henry IV, the immediate challenge, of course, is to oppose this great Scottish invasion.
sentences.zh: 但在他们决定如何对付亨利四世之前，眼前的挑战当然是抵御这场大规模的苏格兰入侵。

sentences.en: So what Hotspur does is he raises the forces of the Perseys.
sentences.zh: 所以霍茨珀召集了珀西家族的军队。

sentences.en: And he's told that the Earl of Douglas has sacked Newcastle, stripped it bare, and is heading back north up the Great Road towards the Tweed and Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他得知道格拉斯伯爵已经洗劫了纽卡斯尔，将其洗劫一空，正沿着通往特威德河和苏格兰的大路向北撤退。

sentences.en: And what Hotspur does is to draw up his men in the shadow of this great Iron Age hillfort called Humbleton Hill, blocking the road north to the Tweed.
sentences.zh: 霍茨珀将他的士兵部署在名为汉布尔顿山的铁器时代山堡阴影下，封锁了通往特威德河的北上之路。

sentences.en: And again, Dominic, I've had an absolute, absolute time of it recently with early 15th century battlefields, because I went and visited this as well just a few days ago.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我最近对15世纪初的战场简直是着了迷，因为几天前我刚去参观过这里。

sentences.en: It's very, very dramatic.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常震撼。

sentences.en: You've been walking the ground.
sentences.zh: 你实地考察过了。

sentences.en: I have been walking the ground like my brother does when he goes off to Dunkirk or Arnhem or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我像我兄弟去敦刻尔克或阿纳姆那样，实地走了一遍。

sentences.en: So I went off to Humbleton Hill.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了汉布尔顿山。

sentences.en: And when Douglas sees the English lined up in front of him,
sentences.zh: 当道格拉斯看到英国人在他面前列阵时，

sentences.en: he withdraws up into the foothills of this Iron Age hillfort and kind of sits there and waits for the English to disperse.
sentences.zh: 他撤退到这座铁器时代山堡的山脚下，坐在那里等待英国人散去。

sentences.en: But the problem for him is that Percy has an enormous number of longbowmen.
sentences.zh: 但他面临的问题是，珀西拥有大量的长弓手。

sentences.en: And so the longbowmen just line up and fire volley after volley after volley at the Scots up on their hill and completely wipes them out.
sentences.zh: 于是长弓手们排成一列，向山上的苏格兰人射出一轮又一轮的箭雨，彻底歼灭了他们。

sentences.en: So a chronicler describes the Scots as looking like a hedgehog.
sentences.zh: 一位编年史家形容苏格兰人看起来像只刺猬。

sentences.en: They've got so many kind of arrows sticking out of them.
sentences.zh: 他们身上插满了箭。

sentences.en: And essentially the entire army is wiped out.
sentences.zh: 基本上整支军队都被消灭了。

sentences.en: There's a desperate charge at the end as, you know, led by Douglas, but it doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 最后由道格拉斯领导了一次绝望的冲锋，但没能成功。

sentences.en: Douglas gets hit in the eye, loses an eye.
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯眼睛中箭，失去了一只眼睛。

sentences.en: A thousand prisoners are taken, including Douglas.
sentences.zh: 一千名俘虏被俘，包括道格拉斯。

sentences.en: And again, a chronicler celebrates this and says the flower of the fighting men of the whole realm of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 同样，一位编年史家对此大加赞赏，称其为苏格兰全境战斗人员的精华。

sentences.en: So it's a brilliant, brilliant victory.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场辉煌、辉煌的胜利。

sentences.en: And for Henry IV, of course, you know, this is a rare bit of good news.
sentences.zh: 对于亨利四世来说，当然，你知道，这难得是个好消息。

sentences.en: He's had all these kind of troubles all over his kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他的王国到处都是麻烦。

sentences.en: So this great victory of the Scots, fabulous.
sentences.zh: 所以这场对苏格兰人的大胜，太棒了。

sentences.en: Or is it?
sentences.zh: 真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Because even here it kind of goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 因为即使在这里，事情也出了岔子。

sentences.en: Because the fact that all these prisoners have been taken on one level is wonderful because it's a source of income.
sentences.zh: 因为俘虏了这么多人，从某种程度上来说是件好事，因为这是一笔收入来源。

sentences.en: They can now be ransomed off and this money can then be used to fight the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 他们现在可以被赎回，这些钱可以用来对付威尔士人。

sentences.en: Yeah, because it's expensive to fight wars.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为打仗很花钱。

sentences.en: So fighting the Welsh is really expensive.
sentences.zh: 所以对付威尔士人真的很贵。

sentences.en: And also there's been a visit to England by, amazingly, a Roman emperor, the emperor of Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 而且令人惊讶的是，一位罗马皇帝，君士坦丁堡的皇帝，还访问了英国。

sentences.en: Manuel II.
sentences.zh: 曼努埃尔二世。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So the first visit to Britain by a Roman emperor since the 4th century.
sentences.zh: 这是自4世纪以来罗马皇帝首次访问英国。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: That is amazing.
sentences.zh: 那真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Henry IV had an amazing life.
sentences.zh: 亨利四世的一生真是不可思议。

sentences.en: Went off to the Baltic, went to Jerusalem, welcomed a Roman emperor.
sentences.zh: 去过波罗的海，去过耶路撒冷，迎接过罗马皇帝。

sentences.en: Had an ostrich.
sentences.zh: 还养过一只鸵鸟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Interfered with the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 干预过威尔士事务。

sentences.en: I mean, an incredible career.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真是辉煌的生涯。

sentences.en: Anyway, continue.
sentences.zh: 总之，继续吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So that had been very expensive.
sentences.zh: 所以那次访问非常昂贵。

sentences.en: And now he's got this rebellion in the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 现在他又面临威尔士人的叛乱。

sentences.en: So basically, he's got massive financial drain.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他的财政负担非常沉重。

sentences.en: Parliament is resentful.
sentences.zh: 议会对此感到不满。

sentences.en: Remember, he'd come to power saying he wouldn't, you know, he wouldn't be screwing money out of them.
sentences.zh: 记住，他上台时曾说他不会，你知道，他不会从他们身上榨取钱财。

sentences.en: And now all he does is ask them for money.
sentences.zh: 而现在他所做的只是向他们要钱。

sentences.en: Mobs in London are starting to get resentful.
sentences.zh: 伦敦的暴民开始感到不满。

sentences.en: They're turning against the king.
sentences.zh: 他们开始反对国王。

sentences.en: And inevitably, rumours are starting to spread that Richard II is alive.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，关于理查二世还活着的谣言开始传播。

sentences.en: So there's this kitchen boy called Thomas Ward, who's appeared in Scotland, claiming to be Richard II.
sentences.zh: 有个叫托马斯·沃德的厨房杂役出现在苏格兰，声称自己是理查二世。

sentences.en: So Henry IV is facing a host of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以亨利四世面临着一系列的问题。

sentences.en: And at the root of all of them is a lack of money.
sentences.zh: 而所有问题的根源就是缺钱。

sentences.en: So unsurprisingly, when he gets the news from Humbleton Hill, he writes to the Persys and says, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以不出所料，当他收到汉布尔顿山的消息时，他写信给珀西家族说，你知道，

sentences.en: you are not allowed to ransom any of your prisoners without discussing it with me.
sentences.zh: 未经我允许，你们不得赎回任何俘虏。

sentences.en: And you have to send your highest ranking prisoners, including obviously Douglas, to Westminster.
sentences.zh: 而且你们必须把最高级别的俘虏，显然包括道格拉斯，送到威斯敏斯特。

sentences.en: So Hotspur, very resentful of this.
sentences.zh: 所以霍茨珀对此非常怨恨。

sentences.en: He sends seven prisoners, but he doesn't send Douglas because he's, you know, he's really getting fed up with Henry IV.
sentences.zh: 他送去了七名俘虏，但没有送道格拉斯，因为他，你知道，他真的受够了亨利四世。

sentences.en: And he's the kind of guy who, when he gets fed up, you know, he shows it.
sentences.zh: 他就是那种受够了之后，你知道，会表现出来的人。

sentences.en: And even when Hotspur does come down to London, summoned by Henry, he still doesn't bring Douglas.
sentences.zh: 即使霍茨珀被亨利召见来到伦敦，他依然没有带道格拉斯来。

sentences.en: So the king and Hotspur have an absolutely blazing row.
sentences.zh: 于是国王和霍茨珀爆发了激烈的争吵。

sentences.en: And remember, you know, they are old, old comrades in arMs.
sentences.zh: 记住，你知道，他们是老战友了。

sentences.en: They're like old teammates, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们就像老队友，不是吗？

sentences.en: Who've fallen out.
sentences.zh: 闹翻了。

sentences.en: They're old teammates.
sentences.zh: 他们是老队友。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So Hotspur blames Henry for refusing to ransom Edmund Mortimer.
sentences.zh: 所以霍茨珀指责亨利拒绝赎回埃德蒙·莫蒂默。

sentences.en: Henry brushes this accusation aside, but it's clear that he has an additional reason now for not ransoming Edmund Mortimer, which is basically that Edmund Mortimer,
sentences.zh: 亨利对这一指责不屑一顾，但很明显，他现在拒绝赎回埃德蒙·莫蒂默还有一个额外的原因，那就是埃德蒙·莫蒂默，

sentences.en: who's stuck with Owen Glendower, has decided to switch sides.
sentences.zh: 他被困在欧文·格兰道尔那里，已经决定倒戈了。

sentences.en: And in November 1402, completely shocking news reaches London that Edmund has married Owen Glendower's daughter, Catherine,
sentences.zh: 1402年11月，一个令人震惊的消息传到伦敦：埃德蒙娶了欧文·格兰道尔的女儿凯瑟琳，

sentences.en: which in turn means that Hotspur is now related by marriage to Owen Glendower.
sentences.zh: 这意味着霍茨珀现在与欧文·格兰道尔成了姻亲。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a twiSt.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这真是个转折。

sentences.en: Both of them are married to, you know, Edmund Mortimer has married Owen Glendower's daughter.
sentences.zh: 他们俩都娶了，你知道，埃德蒙·莫蒂默娶了欧文·格兰道尔的女儿。

sentences.en: Hotspur is married to Edmund Mortimer's sister.
sentences.zh: 霍茨珀娶了埃德蒙·莫蒂默的妹妹。

sentences.en: So, you know, this isn't looking good for Henry IV at all.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这对亨利四世来说一点也不妙。

sentences.en: But despite all this, you know, he doesn't want to think that the Perses are going to turn against him.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，你知道，他不想认为珀西家族会背叛他。

sentences.en: He wants to believe that they will stick by him.
sentences.zh: 他想相信他们会支持他。

sentences.en: He can't afford to have them turn against him.
sentences.zh: 他承受不起他们倒戈的后果。

sentences.en: So going into 1403, Henry essentially tries to kind of bribe the Perses back into supporting him.
sentences.zh: 所以进入1403年，亨利基本上试图用贿赂的方式让珀西家族继续支持他。

sentences.en: So on the 1st of March, the Earl of Northumberland, Hotspur's father, is given the earldom of Douglas.
sentences.zh: 于是在3月1日，诺森伯兰伯爵，也就是霍茨珀的父亲，被授予了道格拉斯伯爵的头衔。

sentences.en: So essentially all the Douglas's lands, a vast swathe of southern Scotland, with the implication that it's now the Perses' responsibility to stop faffing around, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上是把道格拉斯所有的土地，即苏格兰南部的一大片区域都给了他，暗示现在珀西家族有责任停止瞎折腾，你知道，

sentences.en: dabbling their fingers in potential rebellion, but to go off into southern Scotland and conquer it for England and for Henry and for themselves.
sentences.zh: 不要再插手潜在的叛乱，而是去征服苏格兰南部，为英格兰、为亨利、也为他们自己打下一片江山。

sentences.en: But to be fair, you could argue that is very smart statesmanship.
sentences.zh: 但平心而论，你可以说这是一种非常高明的政治手腕。

sentences.en: He's giving the Perses a hell of an incentive to stick with him because he's saying you will increase your domain by an enormous margin.
sentences.zh: 他给了珀西家族一个极大的诱因让他们继续追随自己，因为他承诺会让他们大幅扩张领地。

sentences.en: You'll take a huge chunk of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 你们将夺取苏格兰的一大片土地。

sentences.en: I mean, you'll be even more powerful than you are already.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你们将比现在更加强大。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that it's a good offer.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为这是一个很好的提议。

sentences.en: There's a slight problem in Wales where the prince has now come of age.
sentences.zh: 威尔士那边出了点小问题，那里的王子现在已经成年了。

sentences.en: He's now 16.
sentences.zh: 他现在16岁了。

sentences.en: So he has to be given command of the Welsh war.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须被授予威尔士战事的指挥权。

sentences.en: But again, Henry IV is careful not to tread on Percy's toes.
sentences.zh: 但同样，亨利四世小心翼翼，生怕触怒珀西家族。

sentences.en: And so he makes the Earl of Worcester the admiral, the younger brother of Northumberland, Hotspur's uncle.
sentences.zh: 于是他任命伍斯特伯爵担任海军上将，他是诺森伯兰的弟弟，也就是霍茨珀的叔叔。

sentences.en: He makes him the second in command.
sentences.zh: 他让他担任副指挥官。

sentences.en: So basically, you know, I mean, he's got responsibility for the prince.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你知道，我的意思是，他负责辅佐王子。

sentences.en: He's essentially his governor.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是王子的监护人。

sentences.en: And so between them, Worcester and the prince, you know, they're starting to have some successes.
sentences.zh: 因此，伍斯特和王子两人联手，你知道，他们开始取得了一些成功。

sentences.en: There's been a siege of Aberystwyth, a siege of Harlech.
sentences.zh: 他们经历了阿伯里斯特威斯之围和哈勒赫之围。

sentences.en: They managed to relieve those two sieges and they also march on Owen's estates, which amazingly, up until this point, hadn't been burned.
sentences.zh: 他们成功解除了这两次围困，还进军了欧文的领地，令人惊讶的是，直到此时，这些领地还没有被烧毁。

sentences.en: And they absolutely waste them, you know, flatten them.
sentences.zh: 他们彻底摧毁了这些地方，你知道，把它们夷为平地。

sentences.en: So conditions aren't great.
sentences.zh: 所以情况并不乐观。

sentences.en: But Henry IV in London must be thinking, come on, it's going to be all right.
sentences.zh: 但身在伦敦的亨利四世一定在想，别担心，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: The Perses are going to stick by me.
sentences.zh: 珀西家族会继续支持我的。

sentences.en: And to make absolutely sure of this, he decides that he is going to march northwards to join Northumberland in this great war of invasion of southern Scotland.
sentences.zh: 为了确保万无一失，他决定亲自向北进军，与诺森伯兰会合，共同参与这场入侵苏格兰南部的伟大战争。

sentences.en: Before he can set off, he gets very alarming news from Wales.
sentences.zh: 在他出发之前，他收到了来自威尔士的惊人消息。

sentences.en: He's told that Owen Glyndower has erupted out of central Wales, which by this point has been conquered by him and is heading southwards,
sentences.zh: 有人告诉他，欧文·格林多已经从威尔士中部杀了出来——那里此时已被他征服——并正向南进军，

sentences.en: which is the most anglicised stretch of Wales.
sentences.zh: 那是威尔士最英格兰化的一片区域。

sentences.en: It's been under English rule for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 它在英国统治下已经很长时间了。

sentences.en: And messages say, you've got to come to Wales or else we're going to lose the whole principality.
sentences.zh: 消息称，你必须来威尔士，否则我们将失去整个公国。

sentences.en: But Henry ignores these.
sentences.zh: 但亨利无视了这些消息。

sentences.en: You know, he's trusting the prince.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他信任王子。

sentences.en: He's trusting Worcester that they can handle the situation.
sentences.zh: 他相信伍斯特能处理好局势。

sentences.en: He sends them a thousand pounds to kind of boost the fighting fund.
sentences.zh: 他给他们寄去了一千英镑，算是增加军费。

sentences.en: But meanwhile, he remains committed to the invasion of southern Scotland.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他仍然致力于入侵苏格兰南部。

sentences.en: And he writes to Northumberland saying, you know, I'm coming northwards in order to give aid and comfort to our very dear and faithful cousins,
sentences.zh: 他写信给诺森伯兰说，你知道，我正在向北进军，为了给我们要好的、忠诚的表亲提供援助和支持，

sentences.en: the Earl of Northumberland and his son, i.e. Hotspur, of the battle honorably to be undertaken by them for us and our realm against our enemies, the Scots.
sentences.zh: 即诺森伯兰伯爵和他的儿子，也就是霍茨珀，支持他们为我们和我们的王国对抗我们的敌人——苏格兰人——而光荣进行的战斗。

sentences.en: So the prince, Prince Hal, he's fighting in Wales.
sentences.zh: 所以王子，哈尔王子，正在威尔士作战。

sentences.en: Henry IV is marching northwards from London up towards the frontier with Scotland.
sentences.zh: 亨利四世正从伦敦向北进军，前往苏格兰边境。

sentences.en: And on the 12th of July, he reaches Nottingham in the Midlands.
sentences.zh: 7月12日，他抵达了中部地区的诺丁汉。

sentences.en: And there, Dominic, he is given bombshell news.
sentences.zh: 在那里，多米尼克，他得到了一个重磅消息。

sentences.en: Bombshell.
sentences.zh: 重磅炸弹。

sentences.en: He is told Hotspur is not in the north.
sentences.zh: 他被告知霍茨珀并不在北方。

sentences.en: Hotspur has gone to Chester, that kind of hotbed of Ricardian support.
sentences.zh: 霍茨珀去了切斯特，那是理查二世支持者的温床。

sentences.en: And there, Hotspur is proclaiming that Richard II is still alive.
sentences.zh: 在那里，霍茨珀宣称理查二世还活着。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: And is summoning people to join him in a war against the usurper.
sentences.zh: 并号召人们加入他，共同对抗篡位者。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Devastating.
sentences.zh: 太震撼了。

sentences.en: What a twiSt.
sentences.zh: 真是惊天大反转。

sentences.en: That's very George R.
sentences.zh: 这非常有乔治·R·R·马丁的风格。

sentences.en: R.
sentences.zh: R·

sentences.en: Martin.
sentences.zh: 马丁。

sentences.en: So Hotspur has turned against Henry IV, his old friend, his old comrade in arMs.
sentences.zh: 所以霍茨珀背叛了亨利四世，他曾经的朋友，曾经的战友。

sentences.en: It's all going to pieces in Wales.
sentences.zh: 威尔士那边一切都乱套了。

sentences.en: Who knows what's going on in Scotland?
sentences.zh: 谁知道苏格兰那边发生了什么？

sentences.en: Extraordinary scenes.
sentences.zh: 非同寻常的场面。

sentences.en: Listen, if you want to hear the next part of Henry IV, Henry IV Part 2, in fact, and find out how this plays out, the Battle of Shrewsbury,
sentences.zh: 听着，如果你想听关于亨利四世的下一部分，也就是《亨利四世（第二部）》，并了解这一切将如何收场，即什鲁斯伯里战役，

sentences.en: the moment that the young Prince Hal, later Henry V, explodes onto the national stage, you can actually hear that episode right now by signing up at therestishistory.com
sentences.zh: 以及年轻的哈尔王子（后来的亨利五世）在国家舞台上大放异彩的时刻，你现在就可以通过在therestishistory.com注册，

sentences.en: and becoming a member of our much-loved Rest is History Club.
sentences.zh: 并成为我们备受喜爱的“历史余韵俱乐部”会员来收听那一集。

sentences.en: If you don't want to do that, you'll have to wait till Thursday, and more fool you.
sentences.zh: 如果你不想这样做，你就得等到周四了，那只能怪你自己傻。

sentences.en: And on that bombshell, Tom, thank you very much, and goodbye.
sentences.zh: 带着这个重磅消息，汤姆，非常感谢你，再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
